content: Cephalexin is administered orally. Adults The dosage for adults ranges from 1 to 4 grams daily, divided into multiple doses. The 333 mg and 750 mg strengths should be administered in a manner that ensures the total daily dose remains within the 1 to 4 grams per day range. The standard adult dose is 250 mg every 6 hours. For specific infections such as streptococcal pharyngitis, skin and skin structure infections, and uncomplicated cystitis in patients over 15 years of age, a dosage of 500 mg may be given every 12 hours. Therapy for cystitis should be continued for 7 to 14 days. For more severe infections or infections caused by less susceptible organisms, higher doses may be required. If the daily dose exceeds 4 grams, parenteral cephalosporins in appropriate doses should be considered. Pediatric Patients The usual recommended daily dosage for pediatric patients is 25 to 50 mg/kg, divided into multiple doses. For streptococcal pharyngitis in patients over 1 year of age and for skin and skin structure infections, the total daily dose can be divided and administered every 12 hours. In severe infections, the dosage may be doubled. For otitis media, clinical studies indicate that a dosage of 75 to 100 mg/kg/day, divided into 4 doses, is required. In the treatment of β-hemolytic streptococcal infections, cephalexin should be administered for at least 10 days. Directions for Mixing Cephalexin Suspension 125 mg per 5 mL (100 mL when mixed): Prepare the suspension at the time of dispensing. Add a total of 71 mL of water to the bottle. To facilitate preparation, tap the bottle to loosen the powder, add the water in two portions, and shake well after each addition. The resulting suspension will contain cephalexin monohydrate equivalent to 125 mg of cephalexin per 5 mL (teaspoonful). 125 mg per 5 mL (200 mL when mixed): Prepare the suspension at the time of dispensing. Add a total of 140 mL of water to the bottle. Tap the bottle to loosen the powder, add the water in two portions, and shake well after each addition. The resulting suspension will contain cephalexin monohydrate equivalent to 125 mg of cephalexin per 5 mL (teaspoonful). 250 mg per 5 mL (100 mL when mixed): Prepare the suspension at the time of dispensing. Add a total of 71 mL of water to the bottle. Tap the bottle to loosen the powder, add the water in two portions, and shake well after each addition. The resulting suspension will contain cephalexin monohydrate equivalent to 250 mg of cephalexin per 5 mL (teaspoonful). 250 mg per 5 mL (200 mL when mixed): Prepare the suspension at the time of dispensing. Add a total of 140 mL of water to the bottle. Tap the bottle to loosen the powder, add the water in two portions, and shake well after each addition. The resulting suspension will contain cephalexin monohydrate equivalent to 250 mg of cephalexin per 5 mL (teaspoonful). Storage Instructions After mixing, store the suspension in a refrigerator. The suspension may be kept for up to 14 days without significant loss of potency.
